name: MEDA
summary: MEDA, also known as 3-methoxy-4,5-ethylenedioxyamphetamine or as 5-methoxy-EDA, is a chemical compound of the phenethylamine, amphetamine, and EDxx families. It is the EDxx analogue of the MDxx psychedelic and entactogen MMDA (5-methoxy-MDA). In his book PiHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved), Alexander Shulgin lists MEDA's dose as greater than 200 mg orally and its duration as unknown.

fact.en: MEDA swaps the methylenedioxy ring of MMDA for a slightly bigger ethylenedioxy ring, with two carbons between the oxygens instead of one. Shulgin described it in PiHKAL.
fact.zh: MEDA 把 MMDA 的亞甲二氧基環換成稍大的伸乙二氧基環，兩個氧原子之間有兩個碳而不是一個。舒爾金在《PiHKAL》中描述過它。
fact.zhHans: MEDA 把 MMDA 的亚甲二氧基环换成稍大的伸乙二氧基环，两个氧原子之间有两个碳而不是一个。舒尔金在《PiHKAL》中描述过它。
